beliefs.practice: Always read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit or log its value; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.

Use a single shared Mongoose connection (singleton) for the whole Node.js process and configure connection pooling (e.g., maxPoolSize/minPoolSize) rather than opening new connections per request; close the connection cleanly on shutdown.

Enable TLS/SSL when connecting (use the TLS flag or mongodb+srv TLS-enabled URI) and disallow insecure certificates in production; ensure the driver option serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS are set to sensible values to detect dead servers quickly.

Store secrets (DocumentDB credentials) in Azure Key Vault or another secure secret store and retrieve them at runtime instead of embedding credentials in code or environment files when running in production.

Design interaction documents with a canonical, order-independent key for a drug pair (e.g., pairKey = join(sorted([drugA, drugB]), '|')) and persist numeric severity and structured evidence fields to make queries and ranking fast and deterministic.
Create a single-field index on the canonical pair key (pairKey: 1) and/or a compound index on [drugA, drugB] if you store ordered pairs, so pairwise lookups use an index and avoid collection scans.

When you must query many pairwise interactions for a medication list, issue a single query that $in matches the list of canonical pair keys (pairKey in [...]) to leverage the index and avoid N per-pair round trips.

For vector-enabled lookups (semantic search or embeddings), store embedding vectors in a dedicated field (e.g., embedding) and create a vector index configured with algorithm parameters (e.g., algorithm: 'hnsw', dimension: <dim>, similarity: 'cosine', efConstruction: <value>) appropriate for your model dimension.

When creating vector indexes, explicitly set and document the vector dimension (e.g., 1536 for many OpenAI embeddings) and choose index algorithm settings (HNSW efConstruction/efRuntime, M parameter) to balance recall/latency; ensure these settings are applied when you call createIndexes.

Implement client-side retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors and server-side throttling (e.g., handle MongoNetworkError/Timeout and HTTP 429 equivalents from the service); limit retry count and use jitter.

Detect and handle rate limiting/throughput errors explicitly (429), surface a meaningful error to the caller, and consider backing off or queueing operations rather than retrying aggressively when the cluster is throttling.

Use Mongoose schema validation for application-level enforcement (required fields, field types, enums), and where possible use server-side JSON schema validation or collection validators to enforce data quality on the DocumentDB side.

Avoid unbounded documents and unbounded arrays—store a single pair per document (one interaction per doc) and paginate or batch results; if you must store arrays (e.g., evidence list), index or limit their size to avoid document growth issues.

Do not log patient-identifiable medication lists or LLM prompts/responses that contain PHI. If the app may handle PHI, redact before logging and enforce policies to avoid sending PHI to 3rd-party LLMs unless explicitly allowed and secured.

For production readiness, run the database in a multi-region, highly available configuration and pick an appropriate consistency level (session for typical apps, strong only if you need strict read-after-write guarantees) to balance latency and correctness.

Avoid creating many fine-grained collections; use a single interactions collection (sample_healthcare_03.interactions) and index it appropriately so queries across the knowledge base are efficient and manageable.

When you seed sample data, create the required indexes programmatically (createIndexes script) and check the index builds via the cluster tools; include index definitions in migrations so environments remain consistent.
Use bulk writes (insertMany, bulkWrite) when seeding or updating many interaction documents to minimize round trips and use ordered=false to continue on failures when appropriate.

Instrument queries with explain()/queryPlanner and use the cluster's inspection tools (MCP server profile) to verify that the pairwise queries hit the index and do not cause collection scans or high RU/IO.

Rate-limit and debounce LLM calls from the agent (LangChain/OpenAI) and cache common analysis results (e.g., severity assessments for a given pairKey) in the DB with TTL or explicit invalidation to avoid repeated costly LLM requests.

Store LLM-derived textual assessments separately from structured severity fields; keep a numeric severity field for ranking (e.g., severityScore: 0-100) so you can sort and paginate efficiently without full-text or LLM calls.

Prefer application-level ranking and deterministic heuristics for primary sorting (numeric severity, recency, evidence count) and use the LLM only to augment or justify rankings, to minimize nondeterminism and cost.

Avoid multi-document transactions for the knowledge base unless strictly necessary; if doing multi-document updates you must verify the MongoDB API version supports transactions and be aware of transactional limits on the managed service.

Protect application logs, stack traces, and error handlers from exposing the DocumentDB URI, credentials, or raw LLM prompts; sanitize any error objects that may contain database error messages or payloads before persisting or displaying.
